notes.text:
Using n1 and the qualified grants, the rational mixed-multiplicity kernel extends to a symmetric bounded n-form F. Its pairing with bounded discontinuous D tests follows from a proved directed-continuous Radon integral lemma, rather than generic measurable-net monotone convergence.

Simultaneous superficial choices for all three conditional-Cauchy tuples preserve the same arbitrary mixed slots through each quotient. R(Z) preserves dimension and composition-series lengths. Embedded, nonpure and nonreduced quotients are allowed; finite annihilators are retained. Conditional Cauchy implies full Hölder by a finite integer-simplex maximum argument, then Minkowski and signed quadratic positivity imply energy concavity.

Define F_infinity as the supremum of truncation forms, E(u)=-F_infinity(u^[n])/n, and E1 by finite diagonal value. The truncation supremum equals the supremum over all continuous C majorants. First, bounded approximations decreasing to finite-energy targets are proved to converge without a common sup bound: target diagonal sizes control the negative-shift error. Only afterwards does Minkowski prove E1 cone closure, and approximation passes bounded additivity to unbounded additivity.

Dense gauge-difference tests and Hölder mass bounds define canonical finite Radon mixed measures. Extended pairing gives integral(-v) mu(u1,...,up)=F_infinity(v,u1,...,up), with Hölder integrability. Full decreasing E1 nets require specified limits; for a specified D limit, uniformly bounded diagonal energies are exactly the finite-energy criterion. Relative energy telescopes to E(u)-E(w), and variation is its mixed-measure integral.

Primary change has exactly one measure factor: mu_b=T_*[v(b) mu_a]. Variable cuts max(u,-k v(b)) are squeezed between cofinal constant cuts, proving unbounded energy invariance. Normalization uses actual residue degrees, including inseparability, and only top-dimensional degree contributions; class descent still requires constancy on every full conductor fibre.

At a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, n>=2, nef-Cartier order equals all-semivaluation order. Uniformly negative continuous majorants admit primary Cartier majorants converging uniformly from above. B341's bounded BFJ comparison and BFJ4.6 identify their form values. Thus F_infinity equals minus the exact BFJ Definition4.3 intersection, and E1 equals its finite-self-intersection convention. BFJ itself does not name E1. BFJ4.4 yields decreasing-net continuity; 4.8 alone is sequential. DVR and empty cases are direct.

Complete arguments are whole-proof.md Sections 5–9. No increasing-D closure or unproved infimum-membership assertion is used.

notes.summary: Independently proved the ROOT346 Borel/nonpolar/capacity/comparison extension and repaired its branch-admissible polar reduction.
notes.detailedSummary: Actual bounded-D representations prove the product-test algebra; full form continuity justifies moving tests and Borel maximum locality. Fixed tests establish finite-energy nonpolar cutoffs and canonical truncation TV bounds. Comparison and capacity convergence yield genuine open exceptional sets and quasicontinuity without Choquet-above assumptions. Entire bottom top-dimensional branches remain excluded from the polar claim.
notes.text:
For bounded u in [-M,0], qM(t)=t²+2Mt is increasing, convex and nonpositive. Its tangents have nonnegative slopes and nonpositive constants, so finite maxima give genuine C approximations. An actual decreasing C representation gives qM(u) in D. The identities for squares and products therefore make span(bounded D) a product algebra. Full symmetric-form continuity justifies moving product tests.

With w=max(u,v) and Delta=w-v, continuous strict locality gives Delta*(mu_u-mu_w)=0. Product-test continuity passes actual bounded approximations to this weighted signed Radon identity. Dividing on {Delta>=1/m} proves locality on the BOREL strict set {u>v}; this set need not be open.

For finite-energy inputs, keep the bounded-span test Delta*h fixed while all measure slots approach their limits. Reciprocal slices and successive slot replacement prove 1_Uk mu(u1^k,...,up^k)=1_Uk mu(u1,...,up), where Uk is the intersection of {u_i>-k}. Hölder makes input poles null. The cutoff restrictions increase setwise to the canonical measure. Tail estimates give diagonal TV at most 2A(u)^n/k and mixed TV at most 2(sum A_i)(product A_i)/k. These bounds concern canonical truncations, not arbitrary nets.

Capacity is the supremum of mu(phi^[p]) over -1<=phi<=0. Cutoffs give diagonal capacity absolute continuity; a positive mixed-measure expansion gives the mixed version. Comparison uses Borel strict locality, scalar mass order, the retained equality-locus term and positive reference-curvature expansion. Canonical TV justifies its changing Borel cutoff sets. For decreasing E1 nets, the integrable gap I_lambda tends to zero and Cap{gap>2epsilon}<=2I_lambda/epsilon^n. Actual C representations provide OPEN exceptional gap sets, yielding quasicontinuity without assuming Choquet compact-above regularity.

The broader polar reduction follows from the actual G331 inequality g(nu)>=C_nu g(v0) on a normal branch. Passing an actual decreasing representation to z and selecting a finite z(v0) makes every divisorial reference atom finite. Weighted normalization proves that the reference moment is finite exactly when no top-dimensional normal centre is entirely bottom. It includes all E1 functions. The nodal function (-infinity,0) is globally nonbottom but has a pole of positive branch capacity, so unrestricted nonbottom-pole negligibility is false. Lower-dimensional degree zero alone does not establish zero capacity for every image point.

Complete proofs are whole-proof.md Sections 10–13. No arbitrary-net TV, equation uniqueness, whole P12.6 or full Choquet regularity is claimed.
